title: Diff-MN: Diffusion Parameterized MoE-NCDE for Continuous Time Series Generation with Irregular Observations
claim: Existing generators assume regular sampling and output sparse sequences; ours learns from irregular observations and generates continuous high-frequency output.
layout: 3 stacked rows (a)-(c), left-to-right, dotted separators, purple keyword highlights
description: Three horizontal rows, labeled (a), (b) and (c), compare time-series generation settings. Each row runs left to right. A stacked-card panel of training data sits on the left, a blue bell-curve distribution icon sits in the middle, and a stacked-card panel of generated data sits on the right. Arrows labeled Learn and Sample connect the three parts in row (a). Row (a) has regular observations, shown as evenly spaced orange dots on a dashed green curve, and it produces regular sampled sparse generation. Row (b) has irregular observations, shown as few, unevenly spaced dots, and it also produces regular sparse generation. Row (c) has the same irregular input but produces a smooth solid green curve, labeled continuous high-frequency generation. Purple italic words mark the key differences. Dotted lines separate the rows. Headers read Training Data and Generated Data.
caption: Different TSG tasks categorized by the data continuity and sampling irregularity. Unlike (a) and (b), we generate continuous TS from irregular observations, producing high-frequency sequences with richer contextual information.
abstract: Time series generation (TSG) is widely used across domains, yet most existing methods assume regular sampling and fixed output resolutions. These assumptions are often violated in practice, where observations are irregular and sparse, while downstream applications require continuous and high-resolution TS. Although Neural Controlled Differential Equation (NCDE) is promising for modeling irregular TS, it is constrained by a single dynamics function, tightly coupled optimization, and limited ability to adapt learned dynamics to newly generated samples from the generative model. We propose Diff-MN, a continuous TSG framework that enhances NCDE with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) dynamics function and a decoupled architectural design for dynamics-focused training. To further enable NCDE to generalize to newly generated samples, Diff-MN employs a diffusion model to parameterize the NCDE temporal dynamics parameters (MoE weights), i.e., jointly learn the distribution of TS data and MoE weights. This design allows sample-specific NCDE parameters to be generated for continuous TS generation. Experiments on ten public and synthetic datasets demonstrate that Diff-MN consistently outperforms strong baselines on both irregular-to-regular and irregular-to-continuous TSG tasks. The code is available at the link https://github.com/microsoft/TimeCraft/tree/main/Diff-MN.
